chapter: Return to Basie and leaving in 1948
title: Illness in 1948 and finding drummers to replace him
summary: Jones says he left after his wife's death, stayed until Shadow Wilson and then J. C. Heard returned, and recommended Gus Johnson, who stayed to 1950.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: No, I didn't go on my own. I became ill because I had had a personal catastrophe and it just -
Do you care to talk about it or not?

Well, you know that's when I lost my first wife and it didn't dawn on me from November 13th until that particular time in '48 and I said, "Mr. Basie, I'll get somebody." I stayed in there 3 weeks trying to get Shadow to come back to the band.
Shadow Wilson?
Yeh. He did return to the band.
He had been in there when you were in the Army?

Yes, and he came back but after that I still had to go and Shadow didn't stay there and I went and got Gus Johnson in '48. But there was another little drummer in there before then and I don't know where he went, because I got up out of a sick bed to fly all the way to Chicago to make a recording with Basie on his drums - my drums were somewhere. I went to California and then I was sick all
JONES 195

the way into Chicago. Al 's brother, a beautiful little boy that played with Lionel Hampton, and I went to Omaha out to my farm for two days. Then I came back and I stayed for three more weeks waiting on Shadow Wilson. Then I got J. C. Heard to play in Basie's band. We was playing the Adams Theatre.
Oh, in Detroit. Detroit, Michigan, that was.
Yes, but you know I'm in New York now.
What theatre?

The Adams Theatre in Newark. It was a different thing because that's how Baby Lawrence got messed up. You know we usually opened the theatre on a Friday but the Adams starts on the Thursday... Now J. C. only played three shows because I had a concert to do at Town Hall.
With whom?
With an all-star group. Buddy Rich was sitting in the audience; he had just broke his hand or something.
Can you remember who else was in the ensemble?

No, I can't remember that. I had to go back and play with Basie's band. J. C. joined Basie but when they played the Apollo Theatre I played all the shows and J. C. never played one show. I went back to bed. I was going to go to the Medical Center and get in a hospital
JONES 196

for two weeks. They went to Boston; J. C. played with the band 9 days and left. They came to me and said, "Where can I find a drummer?" I got Gus Johnson because I knew Gus and I knew Gus had tried to play bass. I mean, he was a musician and he knew all about it. I said, "Well, you can play in there." I went down to Nol Studio and rehearsed the band. I said, "You got the job." And Gus stayed there till Basie's band broke up, you know, '50 or '51.
Then he went with a small band.
With a small group.
